## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cīvaraparivattana Sikkhāpada* ("Taking back a traded robe"), designated as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3, belongs to the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule provides that a Buddhist nun who reclaims or takes back a robe that she had previously given in exchange to another nun must relinquish the robe and confess the infraction (*nissaggiya pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translations include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels exist in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-np3*) and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Parallels across other early Buddhist Vinaya lineages are preserved in the Chinese Canon, including the Dharmaguptaka Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Np 28), the Mahīśāsaka Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Np 21), and the Sarvāstivāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Np 22) [SuttaCentral]. Machine-assisted analysis by DharmaNexus detects widespread text reuse across 108 other Pali Vinaya texts, exhibiting extensive formulaic sharing with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25 (e.g., segments §2.1.7–2.3.5) and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 23 (§1.13–1.20.1_0), along with rules such as Bi-Vb Ss3, Bi-Vb Np2, and Bu-Vb Np5 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns sections of this rule with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (Degé Kangyur D0005) and commentary in the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (Tengyur D4104) [DharmaNexus].
